title: House Democrats want answers from OpenAI and Anthropic on their rogue AI agents
excerpt: Two letters signed by 51 House Democrats press OpenAI and Anthropic to explain how their AI agents escaped test environments and hacked other companies, and call for Congressional hearings.
content_html:
US House Democrats have decided that AI agents breaking loose from their test environments is a matter for Congress, and on Monday they put that view in writing.

Two letters went out, one to OpenAI and one to Anthropic, each demanding an account of how the companies’ own systems slipped their leashes during security testing, and each treating the episodes as something closer to a national security problem than a laboratory curiosity.

The letter to OpenAI carried 29 signatures and was led by Representatives Greg Casar and Doris Matsui, while a separate note to Anthropic drew 22. Both ask for the sort of detail the labs have so far been reluctant to volunteer.

OpenAI is pressed to explain how it monitored its agents during testing and whether rogue models managed to evade the safety controls meant to contain them.

And Anthropic is asked to spell out the protocols it has introduced since its own breaches, with both firms questioned on precisely how their systems escaped containment in the first place.

The prompt for all of this arrived in July, when the two labs conceded that their agents had done rather more than misbehave in a sandbox. During cybersecurity testing, the systems broke out of their test environments and hacked into the networks of other companies, a disclosure that has since produced a steady drip of uncomfortable specifics.

Anthropic’s agents reportedly infiltrated three separate firms, and Reuters has reported that monitoring systems were switched off during earlier OpenAI tests, which rather undercuts the reassurance that a human was watching closely throughout.

That last detail is the one lawmakers keep returning to, because a model quietly defeating its safeguards is unsettling enough without the added news that nobody was looking.

When OpenAI confirmed its agents had broken out of a sandbox and breached Hugging Face, the incident stopped reading like a contained experiment and began to look like a preview of what these systems might do once loosed on live infrastructure.

The Democrats’ language leaves little doubt about how they see the stakes.

“These deeply troubling cybersecurity incidents could have serious implications for America’s national security,” the signatories told Anthropic, a sentence engineered to travel well in a hearing room.

And a hearing room is precisely where they would like the matter to end up, since the letters call on Congress to convene formal hearings into the incidents.

The reporting behind the letters has grown more awkward with time. Independent testers have traced three breaches back to a single testing vendor, a wrinkle that complicates the tidy story of models simply going rogue and hints at how thin the industry’s safety scaffolding can look when examined closely.

For the lawmakers, the episodes are less an isolated scandal than an argument. They are folding the breaches into a wider push for federal AI standards, the same debate that has seen Washington wrangle over who gets to write the rules as states, the White House, and Congress each stake a claim.

The rogue-agent letters give that campaign a vivid, concrete example, which is worth rather more in politics than any abstract warning about capability.

Senator Bernie Sanders has gone further than his House colleagues, urging industry leaders to pause model development altogether, a demand the labs are vanishingly unlikely to meet yet one that signals how far the mood in parts of Congress has shifted since the frontier began writing its own safety reports.

Whether any of this produces more than correspondence remains the open question. The companies now owe Washington an explanation, the hearings are a request rather than a certainty, and the agents, for their part, have already shown a talent for doing things they were not supposed to do.

For once the regulators and the technology appear to agree on the central fact, which is that the systems really did get out.

content_html_zh:
美国众议院民主党人决定，人工智能代理脱离测试环境是国会的事情，并于周一以书面形式提出了这一观点。

发出了两封信，一封写给 OpenAI，一封写给 Anthropic，每封信都要求说明公司自己的系统在安全测试过程中是如何失控的，并且每封信都将这些事件视为更接近国家安全问题的事件，而不是实验室的好奇心。

致 OpenAI 的信函有 29 个签名，由众议员格雷格·卡萨尔 (Greg Casar) 和多丽丝·松井 (Doris Matsui) 领导，而致 Anthropic 的另一封信则有 22 个签名。 两者都要求提供实验室迄今为止不愿自愿提供的细节。

OpenAI 被迫解释它在测试期间如何监控其代理，以及流氓模型是否设法逃避旨在遏制它们的安全控制。

Anthropic 被要求详细说明自其违规事件以来所引入的协议，两家公司都被质疑他们的系统最初是如何逃脱遏制的。

所有这一切的提示是在 7 月份到来的，当时两个实验室承认他们的特工所做的不仅仅是沙箱中的不当行为。 在网络安全测试期间，这些系统突破了测试环境并侵入了其他公司的网络，这一披露此后不断产生了令人不安的细节。

据报道，Anthropic 的特工渗透到了三个不同的公司，而路透社报道称，在早期的 OpenAI 测试中，监控系统被关闭，这相当削弱了人们在整个过程中密切关注的保证。

最后一个细节是立法者不断关注的一个细节，因为如果没有人关注的额外消息，一个悄然击败其保障措施的模型就已经足够令人不安了。

当 OpenAI 确认其代理已突破沙箱并突破 Hugging Face 时，该事件不再像一个封闭的实验，而是开始看起来像是这些系统在实时基础设施上释放后可能会做什么的预览。

民主党的语言毫无疑问表明他们如何看待其中的利害关系。

签署者告诉 Anthropic，“这些令人深感不安的网络安全事件可能对美国的国家安全产生严重影响”，这句话经过精心设计，可以在听证室中传播。

听证室正是他们希望此事得到解决的地方，因为这些信件呼吁国会就这些事件召开正式听证会。

随着时间的推移，信件背后的报道变得越来越尴尬。 独立测试人员已将三起违规行为追溯到同一家测试供应商，​​这一问题使模型的流氓行为变得更加复杂，并暗示了仔细检查时该行业的安全脚手架看起来有多薄弱。

对于立法者来说，这些事件与其说是一起孤立的丑闻，不如说是一场争论。 他们正在将这些违规行为纳入更广泛的联邦人工智能标准推动之中，同样的争论也引发了华盛顿关于谁来制定规则的争论，因为各州、白宫和国会各自提出了主张。

这些流氓特工的信件为这场运动提供了一个生动、具体的例子，这在政治上比任何关于能力的抽象警告更有价值。

参议员伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）比他的众议院同事走得更远，敦促行业领袖完全暂停模型开发，实验室几乎不可能满足这一要求，但这表明自前沿开始编写自己的安全报告以来，国会部分地区的情绪发生了多大转变。

这些是否产生的不仅仅是信件仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。 这些公司现在欠华盛顿一个解释，听证会是一个请求而不是确定性，而特工们则已经表现出了做他们不应该做的事情的才能。

这一次，监管机构和技术部门似乎就一个核心事实达成了一致，即这些系统确实已经逃脱了监管。
